families.title: Subject and audience
families.scope: The viewer, record owner, and intended audience can differ.

families.title: Indirect disclosure
families.scope: Structure, ordering, dimensions, or summaries can reveal the underlying value.

families.title: Value producers and derivations
families.scope: The rendered expression does not identify every source or transformation.

families.title: Parallel representations
families.scope: A value can have several copies, including outside visible text.

families.title: Runtime DOM ownership
families.scope: Source component boundaries and actual recorder boundaries can differ.

families.title: Lifecycle and changing identity
families.scope: A transition can expose a value even when the settled view is protected.

families.title: Editing and interaction
families.scope: User actions and events can disclose private input or choices.

families.title: Navigation and resource metadata
families.scope: Location, document metadata, links, or resources can carry private data.

families.title: Capture outside native DOM
families.scope: Recorder integrations can emit payloads independently of DOM annotations.

families.title: Control selection and fidelity
families.scope: An annotation needs the right placement, recorder support, and public boundary.

families.title: Verification and attribution
families.scope: A clean replay, accepted patch, or passing fixture can leave a claim unverified.

cards.title: Delegated access changes the subject
cards.cues: A person can switch workspaces, act as a delegate, or view the same profile form from an admin route.
cards.trace: Join the session actor, selected record, and organization relationship using the route and query. Identify which fields concern the viewer and which concern somebody else.
cards.treatment: Protect private values while ownership is unresolved. Record the open category distinction and the evidence needed to settle it.
cards.counterexample: A staff member editing their own profile through the same form is the subject of those fields.
cards.verify: Compare two authorized roles using distinct synthetic identities and confirm that the decision follows the record subject.

evidence.scope: The Documenso signing title's audience was corrected using the sender/recipient query. Several Akaunting organization labels remained disputed.

cards.title: Private preview shares a public renderer
cards.cues: A public page, draft preview, and signed review link render a common component with similar props.
cards.trace: Follow the publication condition and each route's query. Identify which fields, versions, and people the general audience can actually see.
cards.treatment: Keep confirmed public fields clear in the published context. Protect private fields and draft or restricted variants at their actual destinations.
cards.counterexample: A published profile can deliberately expose a display name while its preview also contains an internal note.
cards.verify: Use a public revision and an unpublished revision with different markers. Check the preview route and public endpoint independently.

cards.title: A record contains several subjects
cards.cues: A thread, timeline, or combined record displays messages, draft notes, automated notices, and imported metadata together.
cards.trace: Identify author, subject, and audience per entry or field. An operator's typed search and the customer address it returns have different producers and subjects.
cards.treatment: Carry each supported classification to its own destination. If a shared boundary protects several private entries, verify what fixed controls it also affects.
cards.counterexample: A fixed service announcement can be public in the same list as an operator's draft and a customer's reply.
cards.verify: Use separate markers per subject and a fixed announcement. Confirm which channels each entry contributes.

evidence.scope: The Twenty comparison found a disagreement over the operator's typed search category. Both reviews required masking.

cards.title: A summary exposes a narrow group
cards.cues: A count, subtotal, percentage, or empty-state indicator is computed from a filtered set of private records.
cards.trace: Determine whose records are in the denominator, what the viewer already sees, and what changing one person's state does to the output.
cards.treatment: Protect a summary when its recorded value discloses a private fact. Review its number, heading, empty state, and associated tooltip or link independently.
cards.counterexample: A published all-catalog item count can be public even when an adjacent per-customer total is private.
cards.verify: Vary membership in a small synthetic cohort and check what survives in text, attributes, and emitted structural changes.

cards.title: Order and presence encode a private state
cards.cues: Row order, badge styling, enabled actions, or the presence of a section changes when a record property changes.
cards.trace: Read the predicate, comparator, or style mapping. Ask whether a recording can associate the change with a person or record even after text is masked.
cards.treatment: Protect the smallest recorded structure or interaction that reveals the condition. Check retained position, classes, and surrounding public context.
cards.counterexample: Alphabetical order over a published directory and an invariant decorative badge may remain public.
cards.verify: Keep visible strings fixed while changing a private predicate. Compare emitted structure and events under the exact recorder configuration.

cards.title: Length and dimensions survive masking
cards.cues: A field uses length-preserving masking, grows to fit its content, or leaves a measured block placeholder.
cards.trace: Identify dimensions or masked lengths influenced by the value and check what the deployed recorder emits. Include nearby elements whose positions change with the private content.
cards.treatment: Use protection sufficient for the relevant disclosure. Where fixed geometry or recorder configuration is needed, document its scope and fidelity cost.
cards.counterexample: A verified fixed-size placeholder can preserve placement while revealing no content-dependent dimension within the tested states.
cards.verify: Compare different-length synthetic values and raw events. Use a browser for claims about real layout.

evidence.scope: In the Twenty DOM emulator, two API key lengths yielded different masked input lengths before blocking. Actual browser geometry was outside the test.

cards.title: A schema supplies labels and values
cards.cues: A registry maps field descriptors to renderers, and the immediate template only refers to a generic field or value.
cards.trace: Find the active descriptors, value producer, and renderer implementation for each mode. Determine whether labels and option captions are fixed configuration or user-authored records.
cards.treatment: Classify and place protection from the resolved bindings. If the schema or renderer is unavailable, name that dependency and record unresolved decisions at the affected destinations.
cards.counterexample: A public product filter can use the same field factory as a private integration settings editor.
cards.verify: Exercise representative descriptor types and confirm which values, attributes, and interactions the native renderer produces.

evidence.scope: The Chatwoot review left dynamic integration forms unresolved pending catalog and FormKit implementation evidence.

cards.title: Fallbacks switch the value's meaning
cards.cues: An empty, invalid, or unavailable value selects another expression for a placeholder, suggestion, preview, or error.
cards.trace: Follow the selection predicate and each fallback producer. Determine whether any branch carries stored data, input, or a fixed instruction, and where each branch renders.
cards.treatment: Protect private branches at every destination. Record the fidelity cost if a verified shared boundary also hides a fixed fallback.
cards.counterexample: A fixed instruction can stay public while a record-derived default shown in the same place is private.
cards.verify: Start populated, clear the field, supply an invalid value, and restore it. Inspect the emitted destination for every supported branch.

evidence.scope: The Twenty emulator recorded a private placeholder in the hidden autogrow measurement copy before the follow-up. The malformed email fallback was exercised separately.

cards.title: A transformation retains identifying information
cards.cues: The UI truncates, formats, hashes, aliases, or abbreviates a value before placing it in text or an attribute.
cards.trace: Identify retained fragments, whether the output repeats across records or sessions, and what other visible fields let an observer associate it with a subject.
cards.treatment: Protect a derived value that still reveals a private fact or stable private reference. Check full-value copies and interpolation sites separately.
cards.counterexample: A fixed synthetic example or a label independently intended for public display can use the same formatting helper.
cards.verify: Compare multiple inputs and repeated visits. Check whether the serialized representation changes with or consistently identifies the underlying private record.

cards.title: A child fetches its own records
cards.cues: A dialog, row, or page title receives only an ID, visibility flag, or callback at the parent call site.
cards.trace: Follow the child through its context, store, route state, or query hooks. Identify the loaded record and descend to each element that emits its fields.
cards.treatment: Classify child destinations from their producer evidence. Keep fixed parent controls clear where possible and track destinations absent from the structural inventory.
cards.counterexample: A help dialog can receive the same open flag and callback while rendering fixed copy.
cards.verify: Open the child with distinct synthetic records. Inspect loading, resolved, and portal content and identify any dynamically created output.

evidence.scope: The Documenso follow-up added missed title, hover, recipient, autocomplete, and inferred-recipient destinations loaded inside children.

cards.title: Accessible names reference separate nodes
cards.cues: A field sets a title, accessible name, description, or live announcement. Its visible text may already be masked.
cards.trace: Trace literal attributes and ID references such as `aria-labelledby` to their source and referenced node. Check where tooltip and announcement content is mounted.
cards.treatment: Protect private text and attributes at the destinations the recorder serializes. Preserve fixed instructions and relationships where possible.
cards.counterexample: A static accessibility label such as Search can stay clear beside a record-derived field value.
cards.verify: Inspect attributes, referenced text nodes, tooltip mounts, and announcements before and after a value or focus change.

cards.title: Styles carry private values
cards.cues: A renderer populates style properties, generated text, class names, or background images from record data.
cards.trace: Identify which style attribute, stylesheet rule, CSS variable, or referenced attribute contains the value. Check the recorder's support for these channels and for style mutations.
cards.treatment: Protect the actual carrier with a supported control. If a shared stylesheet is captured independently, verify a recorder or application-level control for that channel.
cards.counterexample: A fixed icon class and a public branding image can use the same style mechanism without conveying private data.
cards.verify: Change a private style input and inspect emitted attributes, rule changes, and URLs independently.

cards.title: An editor mirrors source into several views
cards.cues: A rich editor has editable content, a source tab, a preview pane, or a read-only representation after save.
cards.trace: Follow the model and submitted value into each native control, contenteditable mount, rendered preview, and error or confirmation echo. Include asynchronous plugins that mount outside the editor.
cards.treatment: Apply supported protection per output. Preserve fixed toolbar labels where the boundary and interaction channel permit.
cards.counterexample: The same editor can render a published help article in read-only mode and a private draft in another context.
cards.verify: Edit, preview, save, and reopen with synthetic text and a private URL. Inspect each emitted carrier separately.

evidence.scope: The Chatwoot source review followed rich-editor content to its mount. It did not verify editor recordings.

cards.title: A hidden sibling measures private content
cards.cues: An autosizing field copies the selected content into a visually hidden node used to measure height or width.
cards.trace: Read the measurement expression, including value and placeholder selection. Resolve the measuring node and its ancestry independently of the primary field.
cards.treatment: Apply the required control to each private copy while preserving unannotated callers and existing layout behavior. Document loss if the same boundary covers fixed placeholder text.
cards.counterexample: A fixed public example in the same shared autosizing component can retain its measurement text.
cards.verify: Check initial, changed, empty, placeholder, and restored states in snapshots and mutations at the measurement node.

evidence.scope: The Twenty autogrow sibling exposed private measurement text in a snapshot and mutation. The follow-up covered exercised value and placeholder states in the DOM emulator.

cards.title: One component renders several native hosts
cards.cues: A field accepts a slot, render function, or element type and chooses different hosts for edit, view, or error modes.
cards.trace: Follow privacy and styling props through each slot, alias, or branch to the final host. Inspect native descendants and where the value actually lives.
cards.treatment: Place protection on supported hosts for all private modes. Keep placement unresolved when a renderer or forwarding definition is unavailable.
cards.counterexample: A shared styled native element can forward the same privacy attribute in every mode when its implementation establishes that behavior.
cards.verify: Toggle each mode and inspect the emitted attribute, protected value, and any public branch using the same renderer.

cards.title: An embedded root has its own capture boundary
cards.cues: An iframe, web component, or separately mounted application contains a private record or interactive tool.
cards.trace: Identify the actual document or shadow root, how content enters it, and whether an outer recorder or separate integration can capture that content.
cards.treatment: Verify the control honored at each capture boundary. Check frame URLs or host metadata even when internal content capture is disabled.
cards.counterexample: An embedded fixed public illustration can use the same hosting mechanism while carrying no private content.
cards.verify: Inspect emitted roots and mutations for the host and embedded content. Include the enabled and disabled modes that the deployment actually supports.

cards.title: Overlays mount outside the annotated ancestor
cards.cues: A tooltip, dropdown, modal, toast, or menu moves its content to a portal or independently managed root.
cards.trace: Read how the UI obtains the value and mounts each instance. Verify actual ancestry for closed, open, and remounted states.
cards.treatment: Protect the private overlay destination separately if the call-site boundary cannot reach it. Keep the trigger and fixed controls clear when they carry no private value.
cards.counterexample: A native child inside the same DOM subtree can inherit a verified ancestor control.
cards.verify: Open, close, and reopen the overlay. Inspect additions and updates using the overlay's recorded identity.

evidence.scope: Twenty proposals traced private email links through the overflow portal. The runtime fixture did not exercise that parent route.

cards.title: Public and private callers share a renderer
cards.cues: A shared badge, link, avatar, or field shows different kinds of data depending on which feature calls it.
cards.trace: Inspect representative callers, prop shapes, and the shared implementation. Resolve the native destination for private uses and establish what the public uses intentionally disclose.
cards.treatment: Choose a private call-site boundary or explicit privacy prop. Annotate the shared implementation globally only when the affected destinations all require it or the documented fidelity tradeoff is accepted.
cards.counterexample: A public support address and a private customer email can both render with the same link component.
cards.verify: Compare both callers across initial values, updates, and fallbacks.

evidence.scope: Twenty's shared email fixture preserved public text and URLs while protecting exercised private variants. The fixture supplied the privacy prop directly.

cards.title: Initial markup precedes the client boundary
cards.cues: Server rendering, streaming, or bootstrap markup is visible before hydration installs client behavior.
cards.trace: Determine which private data is in the first document and when recording begins. Check whether initial markup and later client renders carry equivalent privacy controls.
cards.treatment: Protect every captured initial destination or verify a recording start policy that excludes it. Check serialized bootstrap data only when an enabled recorder can capture that channel.
cards.counterexample: A fixed public skeleton can appear before an already protected client-rendered record.
cards.verify: Observe the first actual recording snapshot and streaming mutations, then compare after hydration with synthetic data.

cards.title: Previous data survives a record switch
cards.cues: A screen retains cached or optimistic data during query changes, account switches, or a failed save.
cards.trace: Follow record identity, cache keys, and pending or rollback values. Identify which version appears in the main view, overlays, titles, and notices before the next response.
cards.treatment: Keep protection aligned with the data actually displayed throughout the transition. Resolve destinations for the outgoing, pending, and restored records.
cards.counterexample: An invariant loading skeleton without record-derived attributes can remain clear while the query changes.
cards.verify: Use two identities with different markers. Exercise delayed success, failure, and rollback, and inspect the emitted sequence.

cards.title: A transient update precedes protection
cards.cues: Reveal, lazy rendering, node reuse, or an imperative update adds a value before a selector or marker may take effect.
cards.trace: Identify when the destination mounts, receives the private content, and gains protection relative to recorder observation. Check the transition back to the original state.
cards.treatment: Keep the required control in place when the private node or mutation first becomes observable. Use an independently verified recorder control where a native marker cannot cover that timing.
cards.counterexample: A node created with its final supported protection can keep the same boundary across value changes.
cards.verify: Check first additions and mutations and subsequent reuse, as well as the settled snapshot.

cards.title: Editing paths emit different events
cards.cues: A field can be changed by typing, autofill, paste, composition, selection, or a scripted update.
cards.trace: Determine how each supported path changes the native value and which events or mutations the deployed recorder emits. Check validation and notifications that echo the input.
cards.treatment: Apply supported value protection and an independent event control when an event can still disclose the value. Keep fixed validation instructions clear.
cards.counterexample: An unbound demonstration control can show fixed public text, while the same widget can collect private data in a working form.
cards.verify: Exercise relevant trusted interactions in a browser and inspect recorded value and event channels separately.

cards.title: A public caption identifies a private choice
cards.cues: Fixed survey options, lookup results, or keypad buttons display ordinary captions while a selection or sequence carries meaning.
cards.trace: Follow the selected state and events. Check whether recorded target IDs, coordinates, order, or selected classes can be associated with the answer or entered secret.
cards.treatment: Protect or suppress the revealing structure or interaction using supported controls. Preserve public captions when doing so leaves the private choice unobservable.
cards.counterexample: A fixed link to public help can record the same click shape without representing a private choice.
cards.verify: Compare different choices under fixed captions and inspect event sequences and related attributes.

evidence.scope: Chatwoot source review distinguished public keypad captions from a potentially private interaction sequence. Recorder behavior remained open.

cards.title: An action exports a private payload
cards.cues: Copy, download, or drag uses private data while its button displays fixed public text.
cards.trace: Follow the action to its callback, clipboard or transfer data, URL, and filename. Identify what the recorder can observe about the action, metadata, and any confirmation.
cards.treatment: Protect captured private destinations and preserve action behavior. Check separate recorder integrations when the payload bypasses native DOM protection.
cards.counterexample: A fixed Copy button can remain visible while its underlying credential field is blocked.
cards.verify: Use synthetic values to check the exact action output and emitted payload separately. State which platform integrations were exercised.

evidence.scope: Twenty's exercised Copy control survived and the real hook passed the exact key to a synthetic clipboard sink. Operating-system clipboard remained untested.

cards.title: Location and route events repeat private data
cards.cues: A route stores a record ID, search term, selected state, or token in the pathname, query string, or fragment.
cards.trace: Follow location writes and determine which location fields, navigation events, or referrers the recording integration emits. Trace the initiating link and global metadata independently.
cards.treatment: Use a verified route or recorder metadata control for any private location value. Protect rendered anchors separately where required.
cards.counterexample: A static public help route can remain in recorded navigation metadata.
cards.verify: Exercise direct load and in-app navigation with distinct synthetic values. Inspect first snapshot metadata and later route events.

cards.title: Document metadata lies outside a component
cards.cues: A feature writes a record name or status into a document title, head element, or route metadata.
cards.trace: Find server and client writers, including shared layout fallbacks. Determine when document-level values change and which recorder channels serialize them.
cards.treatment: Protect or remove the private metadata from the captured channel using a verified control. Keep fixed product or navigation text where feasible.
cards.counterexample: A fixed product title can accompany a private heading because the two destinations have different producers.
cards.verify: Switch records and navigate away. Inspect initial document metadata, updates, and any stale intermediate titles.

cards.title: A link may identify a record or grant access
cards.cues: A URL includes an opaque segment, signature, record key, or slug, while its visible label is ordinary text.
cards.trace: Read the route and access contract. Determine whether the URL grants access on possession, points to a record behind separate authorization, or identifies intentionally public content.
cards.treatment: Block a rendered bearer URL as a secret. Independently classify ordinary private identifiers and protect their URL channel as supported by the recorder.
cards.counterexample: A published product slug can resemble a private record identifier while having a public purpose.
cards.verify: Check the source contract and inspect href, navigation metadata, and any copied form with synthetic values.

cards.title: Media and rich content carry private resources
cards.cues: A link, image, embed, or rendered rich text uses private text, attributes, or resource URLs.
cards.trace: Find the original values and each serialized carrier, including href, src, srcset, inline styles, and embedded output. Determine what sanitization changes and what recorder channels remain.
cards.treatment: Block the smallest native boundary that covers a private resource or unsupported rich-content channel. Protect related text or separately captured resources independently.
cards.counterexample: A fixed public branding image can use the same rendering and sanitization pipeline.
cards.verify: Inspect emitted attributes, additions, and updates. Retain a public resource that uses the same component as a control.

evidence.scope: The Twenty emulator captured private mailto URLs before the source proposal. In the exercised fixture, blocking removed private links and the public caller's URLs remained.

cards.title: Custom event metadata has its own policy
cards.cues: The application sends replay tags, identification fields, or custom action metadata to a recorder API.
cards.trace: Follow each configured payload field to its producer. Establish whether the integration emits it into a recording and whether a transform removes or changes it first.
cards.treatment: Protect private custom metadata at its source or through a verified recorder transform. Resolve DOM placement separately for any copies shown in the interface.
cards.counterexample: A fixed event name such as Help opened can remain if the payload and event timing carry no private context.
cards.verify: Trigger representative events and inspect the complete emitted fields.

cards.title: An enabled integration captures diagnostic data
cards.cues: Network, console, or error instrumentation is configured alongside session recording.
cards.trace: Identify the deployed plugins, allowlists, and transformations. Check which request paths, headers, bodies, exceptions, or log arguments enter recording payloads and when.
cards.treatment: Use the applicable application or recorder filtering controls for captured private diagnostic values. A DOM decision covers only the destinations within its verified scope.
cards.counterexample: A value used only in server processing may have no recording destination when no enabled integration emits it.
cards.verify: Exercise synthetic success and failure paths under deployment settings. Check exact recorded diagnostic fields rather than the developer console alone.

cards.title: Pixel capture bypasses text masking
cards.cues: A chart, map, canvas, screen share, or screenshot can display private values outside ordinary text nodes.
cards.trace: Determine whether recorder plugins collect drawing commands, pixels, frames, hover text, or surrounding DOM. Locate any separately rendered labels or accessibility content.
cards.treatment: Protect private graphics and independent overlays through verified controls for each enabled capture path. Preserve fixed controls and public legends where possible.
cards.counterexample: A decorative canvas can contain public content, and a disabled pixel capture plugin leaves independently recorded labels to review.
cards.verify: Compare raw graphics events and overlays across synthetic private and public cases, using actual recorder options.

cards.title: Prop merges drop or override protection
cards.cues: A component accepts outer props, nested native props, defaults, or a computed class alongside an existing privacy marker.
cards.trace: Read spread and merge order and locate the native receiver. Check whether defaults, slot props, or state-specific classes replace a stronger control or place it on a different element.
cards.treatment: Forward protection through the supported API and preserve stronger existing controls. Resolve any duplicate or contradictory values at the actual native destination.
cards.counterexample: A styled native element can forward extra props as intended when the implementation and DOM confirm it.
cards.verify: Inspect final native attributes in every relevant branch.

evidence.scope: Twenty source proposals followed nested props after finding that TextInput does not forward arbitrary top-level attributes to the input.

cards.title: A control has recorder-specific scope
cards.cues: A recorder recognizes a marker, class, selector, option, or adapter setting that appears to provide privacy protection.
cards.trace: Identify the exact implementation and deployment configuration. Check precedence, inheritance, text and attribute support, and which events and embedded roots are handled.
cards.treatment: Choose controls whose demonstrated scope covers every private carrier. Keep independent channels open when support is unknown or configuration is unavailable.
cards.counterexample: Two integrations can use the same word mask while applying it to different attributes or event types.
cards.verify: Run an exercised positive and private case for each relevant channel under the same deployment settings.

cards.title: A wrapper changes function or public fidelity
cards.cues: A new wrapper or ancestor control would cover a private field along with public hints, buttons, rows, or associated labels.
cards.trace: Inspect native semantics, form association, layout, focus, and event wiring. Identify the smallest existing valid host and which public material would share its boundary.
cards.treatment: Use an adequate boundary that preserves behavior and useful public content. Document an unavoidable public loss with its scope.
cards.counterexample: An existing native wrapper containing only a private value may provide the required protection without adding markup.
cards.verify: Check public labels and actions, focus, keyboard behavior, and layout alongside recording protection.

cards.title: Credentials require blocking across states
cards.cues: A field or widget handles passwords, API keys, recovery codes, signed access links, or other values that grant access.
cards.trace: Follow creation, hidden and revealed views, regeneration, and copy or download. Include input events, error echoes, and other outputs carrying the same credential.
cards.treatment: Block each rendered credential destination. Verify separate controls for captured interactions, resource metadata, or exported payloads that the block cannot cover.
cards.counterexample: A fixed documentation sample can remain public once its nonfunctional purpose is established.
cards.verify: Exercise distinct synthetic secrets across states. Check blocked structure, input events, and surviving fixed public controls.

evidence.scope: Twenty's blocked API-key input and its scripted input events disappeared in the DOM emulator. The adjacent Copy control survived.

cards.title: Mask private text and supported input values
cards.cues: A native text node or text-entry control shows or collects information about the viewer or another party.
cards.trace: Locate the element containing the text or value. Check how the recorder handles text, native values, input events, placeholders, and accessible descriptions.
cards.treatment: Mask private text and supported input values at the smallest adequate native boundary. Add supported protection where attributes or event channels remain readable.
cards.counterexample: A fixed prompt or public navigation label can remain clear beside an internal record or private search query.
cards.verify: Check initial content, updates, relevant editing events, and a nearby public control.

evidence.scope: Twenty's malformed private email fallback was masked as text. The balanced preset independently masked input values and selected attributes.

cards.title: Final replay omits an earlier emitted value
cards.cues: The final DOM or playback appears protected, while initial snapshots, mutations, or plugins may have emitted different content.
cards.trace: Connect each claim to the destination's recorded identity and the phase that exercised it. Inspect complete emitted payloads for independently captured channels.
cards.treatment: Report protection for the specific channels and phases with evidence. Track missing emissions or unrelated marker matches as unverified.
cards.counterexample: A scoped first snapshot and identified update event can establish protection for those two exercised observations.
cards.verify: Check snapshots, deltas, and relevant plugin events. Confirm the scorer rejects substituted data from unrelated nodes.

evidence.scope: The Twenty scorer was challenged with unrelated text substitutions and now follows recorded measurement node identities.

cards.title: A recorder preset can hide patch impact
cards.cues: A marker is absent both before and after a source patch, or the patch and recorder settings changed together.
cards.trace: Compare baseline and patched source under the same recorder configuration. Establish that each relevant channel and phase was exercised and distinguish exact values from masked lengths, structure, or events.
cards.treatment: Attribute existing protection and fidelity losses to the controls that produced them. Record the patch contribution only where the comparison supports it.
cards.counterexample: A source block can remove a native node and its events even when a preset already masks its value.
cards.verify: Use matching runs, baseline positives, and public controls.

evidence.scope: The balanced Twenty preset already masked input values. The source block's observed contribution was removal of the key input subtree and scripted input events.

cards.title: A fixture bypasses part of the real flow
cards.cues: A runtime fixture supplies props directly, replaces an integration, or uses a scripted event in place of a platform interaction.
cards.trace: Identify the component and recorder revisions, adapters, omitted producers, and actual events exercised. Tie every result to that execution scope.
cards.treatment: Keep source, fixture, browser, and complete application results explicit. Record which claims still need the real route, platform behavior, or deployment configuration.
cards.counterexample: A fixture that runs a real component and recorder can establish an emitted result for the component's supplied inputs.
cards.verify: Check output and callbacks, preserve public controls, and rerun unresolved claims through their real entry points.

evidence.scope: The Twenty fixture used pinned components and recorder with declared adapters. It did not exercise the production route or operating-system clipboard.
